text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Parliament will hold an extraordinary session on Monday to vote on the prosecutor general's request to strip the immunity of MP Audrius Butkevichius, suspected of taking a bribe. Butkevichius denies the accusations.

- Ten presidents of East and Central Europe will participate in the conference on good neighbourly relations scheduled for the beginning of September in Vilnius, Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas said.
The Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will also attend the conference.
- The country's depositorory published the list of the one hundred biggest firms in the country. Lithuanian Energy, Mazheikiu Nafta and Lithuanian Gas topped the list.
- If foud guilty, the MP Audrius Butkevichius might be sentenced to up to eight years in prison.
- Lithuanian Post reported losses of 1.35 million litas for the first half of 1997.
- Swedish furniture producer IKEA wants to buy into Jonavos baldai.
- Around 200 illegal immigrants flooded Lithuania in the past few days.
- The oil refinery Mazheikiu Nafta saw the biggest economic growth this year. Its turnover during the fist six months of the year rose 171 percent compared to the same period in 1996.
- Lithuania's banking sector operated profitably in July.
- The timber processing industry in Lithuania is dominated by foreign capital.
- Free Independant Television channel reported 3.6 million litas net profit for the first half of the year compared to 2.25 million litas losses in the same period in 1996.
